items.title: Live: Iran's leader declares victory, Kuwait says it's being attacked by drones
items.description: Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei says the Iranian people are the “definitive victors” in the conflict, ahead of peace talks due to begin in Pakistan on Saturday. Follow live.

items.title: Inside the church of the man who has been leading the US through war
items.description: The ABC visits US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's church, whose leaders challenge the legitimacy of democracy and key principles in the US constitution.

items.title: UK deployed military to deter Russian submarines from targeting undersea cables
items.description: The UK has issued a warning to Moscow after revealing its military had tracked Russian submarines operating in the North Sea.

items.title: How the PM's Singapore visit could help Australia's fuel supply
items.description: Experts say visits like Anthony Albanese's trip to Singapore are important in securing Australia's energy supplies. As one observer puts it, "when you don't have the stock, you need friends".

items.title: Two leaders, two very different reactions to Trump's Iran grandstanding
items.description: If you want a basic measure of the difference between Liberal leader Angus Taylor and Nationals leader Matt Canavan, compare their reactions to US President Donald Trump's extraordinary threat this week that "a whole civilisation will die tonight".

items.title: Super fund members claim they were 'misled' after being forced to sell assets
items.description: A superannuation investment option spruiked as offering "choice and flexibility" has been shut down without proper notification, leaving members less than two months to sell all their assets.

items.title: Construction businesses vulnerable to supply chain shock, experts warn
items.description: Contractors, business owners and economists are warning that thousands of construction industry businesses could go bust as a result of supply chain disruptions caused by the Iran War, unless the government intervenes.

items.title: The NDIS's image has taken a beating before — but not like this
items.description: The NDIS's reputation isn't just at risk of coming under pressure, it's well and truly crumbling, write Nas Campanella and Evan Young.

items.title: Indians speak out after Little India announcement met with racism
items.description: Social media posts about the announcement of a Little India precinct in Melbourne are flooded with racist comments, leaving some Indians with mixed feelings about the plan.

items.title: Queues expected as Europe brings in tighter border measures
items.description: Australians travelling to Europe will be fingerprinted and face-scanned at the border from today, as authorities activate a sweeping new digital system designed to track who enters and leaves the continent.

items.title: Warning projects at risk of delay as Queensland suburbs build upwards
items.description: South-east Queensland councils are building upwards in a bid to house hundreds of thousands of new residents in the coming years.

items.title: Animals on wildlife market more likely to carry human-infecting disease, report finds
items.description: Of the 2,079 mammal species traded worldwide, 41 per cent share at least one pathogen with humans, according to new data released today.

items.title: Crows get home against Blues in the wet in Gather Round opener
items.description: The Adelaide Crows send the fans home happy after ending its losing streak by beating Carlton at a packed Adelaide Oval to start Gather Round. Follow live.

items.title: Bulldogs stun misfiring Panthers in big boilover victory
items.description: The Penrith Panthers unbeaten start to the NRL season has been ended in comprehensive fashion by the Bulldogs at Stadium Australia.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: A historical orbit, emotional support animals and a tiny outback town
items.description: It's been a big week in the news. Did you catch these stories?

items.title: How one of the world's best ballet dancers ended up in Australia
items.description: The Australian Ballet helped put David Hallberg back together after a grave injury. He now returns that favour and leads our national ballet company with a new verve and energy.

items.title: How to get the most out of your bath towels — and when to replace them
items.description: Expert tips on getting the most out of your favourite bath towels and when it might be time to replace them.

items.title: People living in vehicles forced to choose between fuel and food
items.description: The high cost of fuel is making it even more difficult for people living in their cars to afford food, electricity and transport.

items.title: Grace Tame Foundation announces closure
items.description: The Grace Tame Foundation, established by the Tasmanian-born survivor of child sexual abuse, has announced it is closing because securing funding is becoming "increasingly challenging".

items.title: Goalkeeper Andrew Redmayne marks 300th A-League game on home turf
items.description: His career began as a substitute for Mark Bosnich almost 20 years ago, now Andrew Redmayne is joining the A-League's exclusive 300 club.

items.title: Families demand refunds for Easter carnival which left 'kids in tears'
items.description: A Melbourne council is investigating an Easter event held at the Werribee racecourse after it was criticised by attendees, who said it felt unsafe, underwhelming and poorly organised.

items.title: Track closures continue in Queensland. Here's what you need to know
items.description: After a week of "chaotic" disruptions, passengers should prepare for further impacts with the extended April track closures to get into full swing.

items.title: King Charles writes 'very different' open letter after NT flood disaster
items.description: King Charles has written an open letter to Northern Territory residents following recent devastating flooding, saying the "increasingly catastrophic effects of climate change are surely a siren-call to the world for more urgent action".

items.title: Gang rapist on the run after escaping custody at Sydney hospital
items.description: A man convicted of gang raping a 14-year-old girl in a Western Sydney park has escaped from custody while at a hospital. Follow live.

items.title: High Court refuses to hear Bruce Lehrmann's appeal
items.description: The High Court was Bruce Lehrmann's last legal avenue to challenge a Federal Court ruling that found, on the balance of probabilities, he did rape Brittany Higgins.
